dataList.content: <... Faust?>
... Ah, Dante.
<Are you still working? Everyone went back to their rooms a while ago.>
... Yes. The backlog is rather substantial.

I am expected to submit 3 months' worth of missing scheduled reports and participate in meetings concerning post-incident measures following the... collateral event in the wake of our mission in the Grand Magasin.
We had only just returned from Sisyphe Tower, and for once the bus had finally settled into something resembling genuine downtime...
But even after everyone had retired to their rooms, Faust remained in her seat, alone, furiously typing away at her device.
<... Are those all... notifications?>
Yes. Various channels have submitted requests for communication.
Even during our brief exchange, little windows kept blooming endlessly across her screen, only to vanish and be replaced by the next flashing square.
Guess I shouldn't be too surprised... given the chain reaction of events we set off with our mission.
<... This is probably the biggest mess we've left behind after one of our missions, isn't it...?>
While Faust is of the belief that the HQ was prepared for such an outcome...
We did cripple the most important facility in a Wing's Singularity production pipeline. Teleologically speaking.
Despite the rather horrifying implications of her words, Faust calmly continued typing, her tone as even and dry as ever.
... Probably not something I could help with anyway.
When Faust noticed that I was still standing behind her, awkwardly scratching at the back of my clock head, she paused for a moment before speaking.
... Though one hopes that this is an unwarranted concern...
You need not worry, Dante. You have not yet deviated from your journey.
<Well, if you say so...>
... No need to go out of my way looking for something to worry about, I suppose.
More importantly, Dante, is it about time for us to begin the preparations?
<Ah, for another Walpurgis Night?>
<Uhm... I'm getting a feeling it's about time, yeah... Hey, are you starting to get a feel for it, too?>
No. I merely wish to verify a personal hypothesis that the Walpurgis Nights exhibit a certain periodicity.
<Oh hey, Hohenheim had the same id—>

Unlike that man's "guess," riddled with ridiculous bounds of logic and insults to the field of statistics itself, this theory is an extrapolation of Faust's esoteric yet concrete deductive reasoning and thought experimentation methodologies.
<... R-right, sorry.>
<Still, didn't you say some time ago that only pure chance dictates when Walpurgis Nights will occur...?>

And I still stand by that assessment. However, I have decided to adopt the perspective that, on a sufficiently macroscopic scale, events that are seemingly of pure chance ultimately exhibit a degree of regularity.

Indeed, one may have no choice but to consign the event to "pure chance," observing along a linear temporal axis. However, if the perspective from which time itself is observed were altered... if, in other words, one were to rotate the aforementioned "axis"—
—I have judged that, while pinpointing the exact moment is still a challenge, it is possible to identify the period during which its potentiality for advent may be observed.
<... Uh, what?>

A more straightforward explication is needed, then. Let us say that, for the sake of analogy, a set of variegated scenarios is equated to a material object "A," and the resonance of its periodicity "B"; now suppose we project "A" onto a hypothetical mirror image whose surface has an uneven reflectance coefficient. From that, we may calculate B's relative—
<Pause.>
<So... if a material object with mass "A" is basically a bunch of scenarios, you project "A" onto a mirror and use the cycle resonance "B" to calculate the value. Did I get that right?>
... Dante.
<Yeah?>
Simply rephrasing what Faust has said back to me does not lend any credence to the supposed notion that you truly understood the material.
... Maybe I should've at least flipped through a thesaurus.
<Look, I'm just trying to understand what you're saying, okay...?>
Simply put, it is an inductive inference extrapolated from the data gathered over previous Walpurgis Nights.
<Then based on that reasoning, when do you think it'll happen?>

It should have occurred approximately an hour ago based on my calculations, which now appear to have led me to an inaccurate prediction. It was one of the reasons I have elected to continue working out here instead of returning to my room.

However, the fact that your intuition also places the coming of the Night close at hand, Dante, lends support to the possibility that my margin of error is minuscule. Once this round of Walpurgis Night is added to the data set—
—it will increase the likelihood of this hypothesis proving true by 0.552%.
<Huh, not as much as I expected.>

It is sufficient evidence that my approach is moving in a favorable direction, no matter how incremental it may be. After all, the process by which a hypothesis gradually matures into a theory is always quite enjoyable.
Well, then... Take the lead, Dante.
... Most of her words still sailed clean over my head...
... but I'm sure I'll find out as we go along, following the scenario to the end as we've always done.
Whoa, this place looks... so distinct from what we'd seen on our previous excursions!
The floor construction consists of sound-absorbing panels... And the interior paths are designed for efficient transportation, enabling unimpeded traffic between the bays and the hallways...

Ooh, it appears that the architect has chosen a high-ceiling construction to most effectively dissipate sound frequencies, while the placement of ambient lights suggests a design philosophy with a particular focus on minimizing eye strain.
One may arrive at a conclusion that, based on structure prioritizing soundproofing, efficient foot traffic guidance, and the general construction, we have just stepped foot into none other than...!
It's got lots of books. Must be a library.
A lib— *cough* Indeed, Sinclair speaks true. It must be a library.
We fought inside a "Book" in one of these past Walpurgis Nights...
Then this isn't just any other library, but the Library, filled to the brim with those "Books"...
Ah, wait! Before you go, Dante... you should add the Library to your itinerary.
... Seems pretty obvious which library she was referring to.
<Faust, can you access the Gesellschaft?>
Yes. No connection issues have been identified. However...

... I have been making efforts to reduce my reliance in recent days, in case similar connection issues occur in the future. Whatever information you would like to request is unlikely to be of much utility, either.
... Clearly, something's been off-kilter with Faust and the Gesellschaft ever since Ryōshū had her turn. And it's true that they've been giving us some pretty useless information, too...
Alright, then...
<Well, then... care to share your own thoughts instead?>

Deducing from the previously observed information and the visual evidence before us, it can be presumed that we have entered the deepest floor of an entity previously designated Impuritas Civitatis: The Library. To be more precise, we are now on its lowest floor, designated "The Floor of History."
Hmmm... Thus we arrive at the Library at last.
I say this is another in the lengthening list of evidence in favor of the incrementally progressive pressure hypothesis we had discussed.

Indeed. It first began with an encounter with an Abnormality, a subject we were all rather familiar with, before progressing to an event outside the Library, and now we find ourselves on the Floor of History within the building itself.
It is very much in the same fashion as the mounting risk we had observed in the scenarios of the former L Corp.; it seems we can safely expect this trend to continue.
<Then what kind of scenario are we about to...?>
As it is set within the walls of the Library, it can be said with confidence that we will be participating in a "Reception."
However, regarding whether we are to play the guests who have accepted the Library's invitation or its librarians... there is no evidence suggesting either way.
Ahh, ahh. Testing. Can everyone hear me?
<...? This voice... I feel like I've heard it before.>
It seems that this voice belongs to one of those who had commented on our combat performance in one of our scenarios in the former L Corp.
This particular voice, I believe, had introduced herself as "Malkuth."
<Ohh... this is her? She sounds ever-so-slightly different this time...>

dataList.title: Patron Librarian of the Floor of History
dataList.content: Sorry, everyone. Normally, I should be out there on the front lines as the Patron Librarian...

dataList.title: Patron Librarian of the Floor of History
dataList.content: But @#$%!, so I can't be there in person right now. One of you is going to have to take up the Patron Librarian role while I'm unavailable.
Suddenly, a loud, auditory buzz cut into Malkuth's voice mid-sentence, disrupting a part of the message.
We'd heard reality hiccup like this often enough by now. I found myself hardly surprised.

... There appears to be a degree of intentionality in how certain information is concealed from us. Perhaps something has contrived to erase the error in question to explain our "insertion" into this scenario.
<Yeah, that seems likely.>
Alas, further curiosities await; what manner of office is this "Patron Librarian," that one among us must take up the mantle in her stead?
One could say that... a Patron Librarian is an individual responsible for managing various aspects of their assigned floor within the Library.
Ohh, kinda like that... that fella with many arms we met at the Food Court?
Yes, a Floor Manager makes for an apt comparison.

dataList.title: Patron Librarian of the Floor of History
dataList.content: But hey, you've all become total veterans at Receptions by now, haven't you? I know you guys have this handled!
P-prithee, hold! What be this "Reception" thou speakest of?
It is the process by which Librarians receive guests invited to the Library.
Speak human, will y—
... By engaging them through physical means.
... Ahem.
So it's basically a fight to the death with a customer-service name tag pinned to it...
So, who are today's guests, then~?

dataList.title: Patron Librarian of the Floor of History
dataList.content: Well... it's not like Angela ever lets me in on anything. I only heard the name. "Dawn Office," I think?
D-Dawn Office?! The very Office sponsored by Stigma Workshop?! That Dawn Office, thou sayest?!

Ghh...! Had I but foreseen this blessed meeting, I would have worn a different badge colección ere we departed! The Dawn Office badge in particular was offered solely as a limited bonus with a Fixer magazine interview, and I am counted among the precious few collectors who possess one! Ah, what truer banner of mine admiration could I have borne upon my chest...!

dataList.title: Patron Librarian of the Floor of History
dataList.content: So there is a Librarian who's heard of them! That's a relief.

dataList.title: Patron Librarian of the Floor of History
dataList.content: I'm not exactly thrilled about being stuck on support duty again like... before, but I'll stay with you until everything is over. So...

dataList.title: Patron Librarian of the Floor of History
dataList.content: Please don't die, everyone. Let's do what we always do, and we'll make it through again.
Her voice was just as energetic as I remembered. Only now, something seemed to have settled into place in the way she spoke—something fuller.
... Incoming, Executive Manager.
Oho.
At last...!
Ah. These people seem rather glad to receive us, unlike Angela.
Master...! Maybe we should keep a little more distance—
... Hmm?
Oho! Young Outis, I see that thou too art struck speechless by the splendor of beholding such famed Fixers in the flesh!
... No, that's not it.
All this pointless chit-chat is killing my excitement, gramps. Let's get this over with, collect the Book of Zwei Association, and get out of here.
Seonbae... shouldn't we at least get a read on them first...?
*chuckle* Philip. You'll snap in half if you wind yourself any tighter.
<Looks like that old man over there's the Office rep.>
Correct! Behold, for thou'rt in the presence of the Representative of Dawn Office—
... Salvador.
Eh? Young Outis, art thou acquainted with Sir Salvador?
No, I've never met him in person. However...
Then... How is it that...
There really wasn't any need to ask how she knew.
That look on Outis's face answered the question well enough.
